title: Jude and the Sigil
premise: Hazel Eastwick, a nonbinary bone-carver who hears the dead through the relics they carve, has survived by staying unremarkable in Thornfell, a mountain country slowly being erased from every map and memory by the expanding empire of Vael. When Hazel's name appears in a century-old book of prophecies, they learn they are the last living key to the Hollow Door—the only exit from a country that officially no longer exists—and that the empire's Inquisitor-General will burn Thornfell to claim it. Hunted alongside Brannic, a disgraced imperial soldier whose loyalty Hazel cannot afford to trust, Hazel must gather the three sigil-bones scattered among the dead of Thornfell before the Door seals forever. In the end, Hazel discovers the Door doesn't lead out but backward into what Thornfell was, and they must choose: escape alone to safety, or pour their gift into restoring their homeland's memory at the cost of never hearing the dead—or the living—again.
about_author: Jude Kavanagh is a former cartographer who spent five years mapping mountain passes across eastern Europe before turning to fiction. They write stories about borders—geographic, linguistic, and personal—from a small house that may or may not be on the right side of one.

chapters.title: The Bone That Sings
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. In the smuggler town of Greymarrow, Hazel carves a dead woman's fingerbone and hears her final secret—a warning about 'the Door.' Establishes Hazel's gift, their careful invisibility, and their network of clients. Emotional beat: quiet competence shadowed by loneliness; Hazel helps the dead but lets no one close.

chapters.title: A Date With Prophecy
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. A dying archivist pays Hazel to carve his keepsake bone, and inside it Hazel hears him reciting a prophecy written in 1823—one that names 'the Eastwick child' and tonight's date. Shaken, Hazel steals the archivist's copy of the prophecy book. Emotional beat: the floor drops out of a carefully ordered life.

chapters.title: What the Empire Erases
chapters.summary: Brannic's POV. Introduces Inquisitor-General Corvane arriving in Greymarrow with orders to 'process' Thornfell's records and people. Brannic, a soldier demoted for questioning an earlier erasure, is assigned as Corvane's clerk. He glimpses Hazel's name on a seizure list and hesitates. Emotional beat: duty curdling into doubt.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Road
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel flees Greymarrow along the corpse-roads only they know, guided by the dead woman's bone. They are nearly caught at a checkpoint and saved by a stranger who turns out to be Brannic, acting on impulse he can't explain. Uneasy alliance forms. Emotional beat: terror laced with the shock of being seen.

chapters.title: Three Bones, One Lock
chapters.summary: Brannic's POV. Reading the stolen prophecy, Brannic deciphers its structure: the Hollow Door needs three sigil-bones held by three dead keepers, and Hazel's own carved bones are the fourth piece—the key itself. He conceals this from Corvane while pretending to hunt Hazel. Emotional beat: the first deliberate act of betrayal against the empire.

chapters.title: The Drowned Chapel
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The first sigil-bone lies with a keeper drowned beneath a flooded chapel. To reach it, Hazel must listen to dozens of drowning-dead at once, nearly losing their mind in the chorus. They surface with the bone and a new understanding: the dead aren't haunting them—they're recruiting them. Emotional beat: awe and dread entwined.

chapters.title: Interrogation at the Pass
chapters.summary: Brannic's POV. Corvane interrogates a village that sheltered Hazel, demonstrating the empire's memory-eating engine, the Pale Engine, which unmakes names and places. Brannic watches a friend forget his own mother. Emotional beat: horror crystallizing into resolve; loyalty redefined.

chapters.title: Ash and Antler
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel seeks the second keeper in the high antler-fields, guarded by a hermit order who remember old Thornfell. Their blind abbess tests Hazel: she asks what Hazel would trade for survival. Hazel lies, and the abbess knows it, but gives the bone anyway—with a warning. Emotional beat: shame meeting unexpected grace.

chapters.title: Two Truths in One Bed
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Trapped by a storm in a waystation, Hazel and Brannic exchange half-truths and, finally, real ones—his desertion, her (their) fear of being a weapon. Attraction deepens even as each hides the prophecy's final clause. Emotional beat: intimacy built on a fault line.

chapters.title: Corvane's Offer
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Corvane captures Hazel—not to kill them, but to hire them: he claims the Door leads to a treasury that could buy Thornfell's survival as a vassal state. His reasoning is seductive, his cruelty casual. Hazel escapes using a dead man's voice to turn his soldiers. Emotional beat: temptation wearing a reasonable face.

chapters.title: The Keeper Who Refused
chapters.summary: Brannic's POV. The third keeper's grave is empty—the keeper refused death and walks still, mad, somewhere in the capital's ruins. Brannic deserts openly, burning his commission, and sends word to Hazel through smuggler channels. Emotional beat: liberation that feels like falling.

chapters.title: City of Unwritten Names
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel enters Thornfell's erased capital, where the Pale Engine's work is visible: streets no one remembers, citizens who answer to numbers. Here Hazel finds the walking keeper and learns the truth the prophecy hid—the Door opens onto the past, not the future. Emotional beat: grief for a country being deleted in real time.

chapters.title: The Mad Keeper's Bargain
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The third keeper will surrender the bone only if Hazel promises to use the Door to change history—to save the keeper's murdered family. Hazel accepts, knowing the promise may be impossible. The keeper's bone burns cold in Hazel's hand. Emotional beat: compassion weaponized into obligation.

chapters.title: Betrayal in the Bone-Vault
chapters.summary: Brannic's POV. Brannic reunites with Hazel at the bone-vault where the Door sleeps, but Corvane anticipated them—their route was leaked by the smugglers Brannic trusted. Soldiers take the sigil-bones; Brannic takes a crossbow bolt meant for Hazel. Emotional beat: trust shattered and proven in the same breath.

chapters.title: What Corvane Wants
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV (first appearance). Alone with the Door, Corvane reveals his true aim: not treasure but authorship—he means to walk into the past and write himself into Thornfell's founding, making the erasure retroactive and eternal. He needs Hazel alive because the key answers only to a bone-carver's blood. Emotional beat: banality of monstrous ambition.

chapters.title: The Chorus Rises
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Imprisoned, Hazel does what no one expects: listens. Every bone they've ever carved, every dead client, answers across distance, feeding Hazel strength and secrets—the vault's weaknesses, the guards' shames. The dead of Thornfell choose their side. Emotional beat: isolation transformed into communion.

chapters.title: Breaking the Vault
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. A wounded Brannic, guided by voices only he can barely hear, springs Hazel during the solstice transfer when the Door thins. The escape costs lives, including the young guard who once showed Brannic kindness. Emotional beat: victory stained with grief; no clean hands.

chapters.title: The Price of Survival
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Before the Door stands open, the prophecy's hidden clause activates: the key requires a carver to give up their gift permanently. Hazel realizes escape means silence forever—no more dead, no more hearing Brannic's heartbeat-honest voice through bone. They hesitate at the threshold. Emotional beat: the theme made flesh.

chapters.title: Doorway Duel
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POVs. Corvane forces the Door with stolen blood as Hazel and Brannic attack. Inside the threshold, past and present overlap: Corvane begins rewriting Thornfell's founding, and Hazel counters by pouring the dead's testimony—every erased name—into the Door's frame. Brannic holds the physical line, bleeding. Emotional beat: desperate, luminous defiance.

chapters.title: The Name Restored
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel makes the choice the abbess foresaw: instead of escaping or rewriting history, they give their entire gift to the Door, speaking Thornfell's true name until it re-inscribes itself on maps, memories, and minds. Corvane, unmade by the country he tried to erase, dissolves. The Door closes forever. Emotional beat: sacrifice as authorship.

chapters.title: Silence
chapters.summary: Brannic's POV. Aftermath: Thornfell remembered, Corvane's machinery shattered, Brannic carrying Hazel down from the silent vault. Hazel wakes deaf to the dead—and terrified of the quiet. Brannic stays anyway, choosing to be heard the ordinary way. Emotional beat: tenderness after ruin.

chapters.title: The Carver's New Trade
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, epilogue. A year later, Hazel carves keepsakes that hold nothing but love, in a Greymarrow that remembers itself. A child arrives asking if bones really sing; Hazel says ask me again when you're older. On the shelf, the prophecy book now ends mid-sentence. Emotional beat: peace earned, mystery preserved, life continuing.
